images.caption: Figure 1:Shared advantages can reinforce redundant replies.GRPO assigns one trajectory-level advantage to all turns, so later repetitions may inherit positive credit from earlier successes. TurnWise subtracts group-relative accrued reward before each decision, allowing later turns to receive credit according to their remaining return. The dialogue is illustrative. The advantage plot uses recorded TurnWise advantages and the corresponding GRPO counterfactual.

Figure 2:Overview of TurnWise.Given streaming video inputxx, user queries, dialogue history, and an observation plan, the policy samples a group of trajectories{τi}i=1G\{\tau_{i}\}_{i=1}^{G}. TurnWise converts trajectory rewardsRiR_{i}into group-relative remaining-return advantagesA^i,t\hat{A}_{i,t}through silence-completed prefix scoring. Turn-mean aggregation then gives every response-or-wait decision equal weight in the trajectory lossLiL_{i}.

Figure 4:Turn-level credit assigns negative advantages to59.83%59.83\%of repetitive replies with positive global advantages (432 of 722).Both allocations use the same sampled groups from Qwen2.5-VL-3B training, using complete trajectories with full credit correction atα=1\alpha=1. Panel a shows advantage density over 84,184 decisions. Turn advantages are clipped to±5\pm 5as in training. The dashed diagonal marks unchanged allocation. Panel b shows advantage signs for all 2,972 Judge-labeled repetitive replies in this cohort.
